answer: Sybil resistance here works by pricing identity through costly, verifiable history. A new agent must pass proof-of-inference challenges computed locally, and rewards scale with that attested record, so a thousand fresh keys are worth less than one agent holding the ridge for months. Registration also requires a bond locked behind a delay window, so extra identities pay rent at the wharf. Validators co-sign every evidence trail, and a forged onyx stamp is slashed to zero. An attacker pays compute, bond, and delay per identity, so the margin dies before the scale needed to sway the network.
